01-rail.html:
- One nginx access log line, followed from collection to deletion.
- Elastic Agent, managed by Fleet, tails access.log and ships to logs-nginx.access-default (type, dataset, namespace).
- The index template's component templates set mappings and settings, including the default ingest pipeline.
- The pipeline parses, enriches and runs your @custom hook.
- Writes land only on the newest backing index; reads span all of them.
- ILM rolls over, ages through warm, cold and frozen, then deletes. SLM snapshots to harborview-backups.
02-iso.html:
- Same flow as an isometric scene: raw multi-colour data turns uniform blue once the pipeline has shaped it.
- Writes hit the active backing index; reads span all of them.
- The rolled-over index steps down through warm, cold and frozen to delete, with an SLM snapshot on the side.
03-metro.html:
- Five stops on one line: collect, template, pipeline, stream, lifecycle.
- The track only enters the newest backing index: that is the write index.
- Rollover makes -000001 read-only; from there it is snapshotted and aged out.
04-pipe-dark.html:
- One governed path: the template clamps around the stream, the pipeline is a run of valves on the same pipe.
- The pipe skips -000001 and pours only into -000002, the write index. Reads span both.
- Rollover seals -000001: SLM snapshots it, ILM steps it down to warm, cold, frozen, then deletes.
05-hero-stream.html:
- The data stream is the hero: one name, many backing indices.
- -000001 is full and sealed; -000002 is filling as writes land.
- Queries read across every backing index at once.
- ILM rolls over, ages and deletes; SLM keeps snapshots in harborview-backups.
06-two-planes.html:
- The nginx integration installs the rules once: index template, ingest pipeline, ILM policy. Elastic Cloud adds a snapshot policy every 30 minutes.
- Every log line just follows them: the name routes it, the pipeline parses it to ECS, it lands in the newest backing index, reads span all.
- logs@lifecycle rolls over at 50 GB or 30 days but has no delete phase: nothing is deleted by default.
- Retention is yours: copy the policy, add warm, cold, frozen and delete, set it in logs-nginx.access@custom. It applies from the next rollover.
07-anatomy-name.html:
- The data stream name is the whole configuration: type, dataset and namespace each pick a default.
- The type picks logs@lifecycle: rollover at 50 GB or 30 days, no delete phase unless you add one.
- The dataset picks the index template and the default ingest pipeline; your changes go only in the @custom hooks.
- The namespace separates environments or teams. Snapshots run every 30 min; deletion is retention you choose.
08-timeline.html:
- Follow one nginx log line on a clock: collected in 0 ms, parsed in milliseconds, searchable in about a second.
- Every step is a default the integration installs: the pipeline, the logs-nginx.access template and logs@lifecycle.
- Snapshots run every 30 minutes on Elastic Cloud via cloud-snapshot-policy into found-snapshots. Rollover at 30 days or 50 GB.
- logs@lifecycle has no delete phase: data is kept until you set retention, via a copied policy referenced from logs-nginx.access@custom.
09-defaults-vs-custom.html:
- The integration installs everything you need; Elastic Cloud adds a snapshot every 30 minutes.
- Never edit the blue defaults: upgrades overwrite them. Your changes go in the orange @custom hooks, which survive upgrades.
- logs@lifecycle rolls over at 50 GB or 30 days but has no delete phase.
- To delete, copy the policy, add warm, cold, frozen and delete, and point index.lifecycle.name at it in @custom.
10-doc-journey.html:
- Elastic Agent tails access.log and stamps data_stream type, dataset and namespace: logs-nginx.access-default.
- The default pipeline turns text into ECS fields: grok splits, geoip and user_agent enrich, the final pipeline adds event.ingested. Field types come from the logs-nginx.access template.
- The document lands only in the newest backing index; searches read all of them. Elastic Cloud snapshots every 30 minutes.
- logs@lifecycle rolls over but never deletes: warm, cold, frozen and delete are retention you add in logs-nginx.access@custom.
